title: Add shared KMS client wrapper library in monorepo (timeouts/retries + safe defaults)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Security & Compliance Foundation — KMS integration hardening + rotation docs
description:
Context
- We currently have multiple KMS call sites across control-plane and data-plane components with inconsistent timeouts/retry behavior, inconsistent error mapping, and uneven telemetry.
- Regulated Private/Dedicated customers are asking for clear failure-mode behavior and audit-friendly operational guidance; reliability depends on not amplifying KMS issues (timeouts/throttling) into platform-wide incidents.
- This ticket implements the shared wrapper library described in ADR-007 so we can standardize behavior across services.

Goal
- Add a shared KMS client wrapper library in the Redwood monorepo with:
  - Explicit timeouts and bounded retry budgets (safe defaults)
  - Standardized error taxonomy mapping (aligned with ENG-4822)
  - Structured logging + metrics/tracing hooks
  - Configuration knobs that are consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
  - Guardrails that prevent dangerous prod configs without explicit override

Non-goals
- No net-new cryptographic primitives/algorithms.
- No cross-platform auth overhaul (IAM is handled in separate workstreams).
- Not implementing rotation workflow itself here (see ADR-008 / related tickets); wrapper must be compatible with dual-read/dual-decrypt behavior.

Proposed library shape (per ADR-007)
- Package location: //libs/security/kms (final location per architecture review)
- Interface (conceptual):
  - Encrypt(plaintext, keyRef, context) -> ciphertext
  - Decrypt(ciphertext, keyRef, context) -> plaintext
  - GenerateDataKey(keyRef, context) -> dek + encryptedDek
  - (Optional, metadata-only) DescribeKey(keyRef)
- Provider implementations (behind interface):
  - AWS KMS first (required for current Private deployments)
  - GCP/Azure shims: interface-compatible stubs to unblock Private installer validation and future expansion; do not block AWS shipping.

Default policy (safe defaults)
- Timeout:
  - Default per call: 2s hard deadline for KMS RPC
  - Separate connect timeout (e.g., 250ms) where supported
- Retries:
  - Retry only on transient errors (throttling, timeouts, certain 5xx)
  - Max attempts: 3 (initial + 2 retries)
  - Max elapsed retry budget: 2.5s total (wrapper must enforce)
  - Exponential backoff + jitter; respect provider Retry-After when available
- Circuit breaker integration is NOT part of this ticket (ENG-4824), but wrapper must expose the required signals (error category, attempt count, latency) for breaker decisions.
- Caching constraints:
  - No caching of decrypted material (plaintext) or raw key material
  - Metadata caching allowed only for non-sensitive DescribeKey-like calls, with short TTL and explicit invalidation hooks

Error taxonomy + observability
- Map provider-specific errors into canonical categories (ENG-4822):
  - AccessDenied
  - NotFound
  - Throttling
  - Timeout
  - InvalidCiphertext
  - DependencyUnavailable (generic 5xx / network where applicable)
  - Unknown
- Required structured log fields (at call boundary):
  - kms.provider (aws|gcp|azure)
  - kms.operation (encrypt|decrypt|generate_data_key|describe_key)
  - kms.key_ref (redacted/hashed; never log full ARN in plaintext logs for Private)
  - kms.error_category
  - kms.http_status (if available)
  - kms.request_id (if available)
  - kms.attempts
  - kms.latency_ms
- Tracing:
  - Child span per KMS call named "kms.<operation>" with tags above.

Config knobs (must be consistent across services)
- kms.timeout_ms (default 2000)
- kms.retry.max_attempts (default 3)
- kms.retry.max_elapsed_ms (default 2500)
- kms.retry.base_backoff_ms (default 50)
- kms.retry.max_backoff_ms (default 500)
- kms.retry.jitter (default on)
- kms.endpoint_override (default empty; used for Private/local testing)
- kms.region (default inferred)
- kms.telemetry.enabled (default true)
- kms.config.allow_unsafe_overrides (default false; required to set retry.max_attempts > 5 or timeout_ms > 10s)

Acceptance criteria
- Wrapper is available to be imported by control-plane and data-plane services; includes README usage + examples.
- Default timeouts/retry behavior is explicitly coded (no SDK implicit defaults).
- Wrapper returns only canonical errors to callers; provider errors are attached as internal details for debugging.
- Wrapper emits metrics/traces/logs using Redwood conventions.
- Guardrails: production config validation prevents enabling unsafe retry storms without an explicit override.
- Security review sign-off from Security Eng (Marcus/Hanae) on log redaction + error detail handling.

Testing
- Unit tests: error mapping (provider codes -> canonical), retry budget enforcement, jitter/backoff behavior.
- Integration tests are tracked separately (ENG-4825) but wrapper must provide hooks/mocks to simulate timeouts/throttling.

Rollout plan
1) Land wrapper + migrate 1 low-risk call site behind feature flag kms_wrapper_v1.
2) Expand migrations across remaining call sites (separate PRs) with SRE watch.
3) Enable by default in staging; then prod canary in one region for Hosted and one Dedicated cell; Private rollout via installer version gate.

Links
- ADR: adr-007-kms-client-wrapper-and-failure-policy
- Related: ENG-4822 (error taxonomy + metrics), ENG-4824 (circuit breaker), ENG-4825 (failure-mode integration tests)

Notes / risks
- Main risk is retry amplification under widespread KMS timeouts. Wrapper must enforce a hard retry budget and jitter.
- Ensure we do not leak full key ARNs into customer-visible logs; use hashed key reference.
- Ensure default timeout does not break legitimate long-tail KMS latencies; monitor p99 and adjust with SRE guidance if needed.
